package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, distributed via Linux repos and bundled in proprietary products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input, causing the library to resolve attacker-controlled URIs. This enables unauthenticated attackers to force the server to make arbitrary network requests, potentially accessing internal resources, exfiltrating sensitive data, or chaining with other vulnerabilities for remote code execution. The flaw is present by default in all affected versions and can be exploited without authentication, making these versions highly dangerous in any security-sensitive deployment.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the application processes SAML/XML input
execution_context.file_location: XML parsing logic in the xmltooling library, specifically during KeyInfo element processing (e.g., xmltooling/XMLTooling.cpp or xmltooling/security/KeyInfoResolver.cpp)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when attacker-supplied SAML/XML input is parsed, the library processes the KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod element, initiates an outbound HTTP request to the attacker-controlled URI, and retrieves or attempts to retrieve the referenced resource, resulting in potential access to internal services or exfiltration of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing untrusted XML input to specify arbitrary URIs for server-side resolution is a classic SSRF pattern. This enables attackers to force the server to make network requests to attacker-controlled or internal endpoints, which can be leveraged for data exfiltration, internal network scanning, or further exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal XML signature or key processing should only resolve URIs from a trusted, whitelisted set or local resources. Accepting and resolving arbitrary, attacker-supplied URIs from untrusted XML input violates secure design principles and exposes the server to SSRF and related attacks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In some legitimate SAML or cryptographic workflows, remote key retrieval via KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod is used, but only when restricted to trusted, pre-approved endpoints. Unrestricted remote retrieval is never safe in production environments.
key_indicators: Unrestricted resolution of URIs from KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements in XML input
No authentication or authorization required to trigger outbound network requests
Parsing of attacker-controlled XML leading to server-initiated HTTP/HTTPS requests
Lack of URI whitelisting or validation in XML parsing logic

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits crafted SAML/XML input containing a KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod element with a malicious, attacker-controlled URI.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library parses the XML and initiates a server-side HTTP request to the attacker-controlled URI.

attack_chain.action: The server-side request can access internal resources, exfiltrate sensitive data, or be chained with other vulnerabilities (such as command injection) for further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential denial of service, unauthorized access to internal network resources, or unauthenticated remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: SAML/XML input containing KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with external or non-whitelisted URIs
Unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests originating from authentication or XML processing services during SAML assertion handling
Resolution of attacker-controlled URIs during XML signature validation or SAML authentication workflows
file_indicators: Presence of xmltooling library versions prior to 3.2.4 in application dependencies or system packages
Application or server logs showing parsing of SAML/XML with external KeyInfo URIs
Configuration files referencing vulnerable xmltooling versions
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains from SAML/XML processing endpoints
Requests to internal network resources (e.g., 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, localhost, or internal IP ranges) triggered by SAML/XML input
Unusual network activity from authentication or SSO services immediately following SAML/XML parsing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML/XML input for KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements referencing external or untrusted URIs. Detect and alert on unexpected outbound network requests from authentication or XML processing services, especially during SAML assertion or XML signature validation. Audit application dependencies and system packages for vulnerable xmltooling versions and upgrade to 3.2.4 or later. Implement strict URI whitelisting or schema validation to block or sanitize untrusted URIs in XML input. Use web application firewalls to detect and block SSRF attempts in SAML/XML processing.
